summary: Kashi Prasad Jayaswal was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied at the University of Allahabad, Jesus College, and the University of Oxford (M.A. circa 1906–1909). In 1917, he served as Tagore Professor of Law at the University of Calcutta.
Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, Kashinath Narayan Dikshit succeeded Rakhaldas Bandyopadhyay and served as Director General of Archaeology at the Archaeological Survey of India in 1937.

Kashinath Trimbak Telang worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Mumbai and Elphinstone College from circa 1864 to 1869, later serving as Senior Dakshina Fellow at Elphinstone College circa 1869 to 1872.

Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat College (circa 1914–1945) and as Honorary Professor of Sanskrit at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (circa 1956–1970).

Kate Crosby is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She has held posts at Cardiff University (attested 2002), the Buddhist Institute in 2003, and SOAS University of London as the Seiyu Kiriyama post holder in Buddhist Studies.
Kate Wharton works in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. from SOAS University of London by 2008 and was affiliated with Birkbeck, University of London in 2010.
Katharina Sabernig, a scholar in Tibetology and history and archaeology, earned her PhD from the University of Vienna by 2017 and held a post at the Medical University of Vienna.
Katherine Anne Narraway works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed her Master of Arts degree at McGill University, where she was supervised by G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Katherine Anne Paul is a scholar of Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Indology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Gudrun Bühnemann and teachers Tsetan Chonjore, Pasang Dhondup, Nawang Dorji, Gautam V. Vajracharya, Rama Joshi, and Geeta Manandhar.

Katherine Janiec Jones specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She studied at Davidson College, completed her PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Paul J. Griffiths, and was taught by William K. Mahony and Karl A. Plank.

Katherine K. Young, a religious studies and Indology scholar, studied at the University of Chicago (circa 1968–1970) and McGill University (circa 1970–1977). She served as Professor at McGill University from circa 1978 to 2017.

Kathleen D. Morrison is an archaeologist and Indologist. After studying at Notre Dame, New Mexico, and UC Berkeley (circa 1987–1992), she was Assistant Professor of Anthropology at Northwestern (circa 1993–1996) and held a post at Pennsylvania (circa 2017).

Kathleen M. Erndl was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She held posts at DePauw University, UW–Madison (circa 1985–1987), Lewis & Clark College (circa 1987–1993), and Florida State University as Associate Professor of Religion (circa 1993–2017).

Kathleen McDonald is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. She studied under traditional teachers Thubten Zopa Rinpoche (circa 1974), Tenzin Gyatso, Thubten Yeshe, Ngawang Dhargyey, Jampa Tegchok, and Ribur Rinpoche.
Kathrin Holz works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Würzburg under Ingo Strauch and holds a research affiliation with the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Kathryn H. Selig Brown specializes in Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Michigan by 2000, where she was supervised by Walter M. Spink.

Katia Buffetrille works in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at Paris Nanterre University (circa 1984–1996, PhD) under Alexander W. Macdonald and held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études in circa 1998.

Katsuhiko Kamimura was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara and V. Raghavan. He held posts at Kokugakuin University (circa 1977–1986) and as associate professor (助教授) at the University of Tokyo (circa 1986–2003).
Katsuhiro Yoshizawa works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Doshisha University from circa 1964 to 1969 and served as Professor at Hanazono University from circa 1994 to 2016.

Katsumi Mimaki specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Kyoto University, INALCO, and Sorbonne Nouvelle/Paris (PhD 1972–1975). At Kyoto University, he served as research assistant (1975–1993) and Professor (1993–2010).
